conceptual assets.information: The stored enable setting that permits SPI operation and controls FIFO clearing, clock generation, engine activation and the clock-enable output.

conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the enable bit to disable the SPI engine, clear queued data and prevent further transfers.

Suppressing irq_o at line 255 can prevent software from servicing pending data and stall integrated operation.

considered, not kept.reason: Their only functional use is shaping the serial clock waveform, as shown by the assignments to rtx_engine.sck at lines 286 and 300 through 324, which the clock rule excludes apart from read-back.
A serial link clock is excluded as a conceptual asset by the clocks and resets rule, although spi_clk_o is produced at line 344.
clkgen_i, cdiv_cnt and spi_clk_en only pace transceiver steps through lines 299, 308, 317 and 371 through 377, so the pacing-pulse rule excludes them as independent information.
rtx_engine.state, bitcnt, busy and done only order or report the serial transfer steps at lines 282 through 340, which the sequencing-state rule excludes as information of their own.
The FIFO availability, half-full and free indicators at lines 160 through 163 and 256 through 259 only report or time buffered data and are excluded by the port-buffer and buffer-status rules.
The settings written at lines 146 through 149 only tune the interrupt output at line 255, so the port-options rule bars them as independent pieces.

The request direction, strobe and address select accesses at lines 137 through 152 and 212 through 246, while the acknowledge and constant error fields at lines 132 through 134 are covered by access-command and handshake-copy rules.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the registers and instances at lines 116 through 130 and 266 through 276, so the clocks and resets rule excludes them.
